title: PRD Draft — Customer-visible Model Release Notes (Console + Feed) v0.7
content:
Doc status: Draft (work-in-progress). Not yet a commitment for GA behavior.
Last updated: 2026-02-24 (Marissa)

1) Problem statement
Today customers learn about model updates inconsistently (docs pages, ad-hoc Slack/email, sometimes runtime notes). This causes:
- Confusion during rollouts/A-B tests (“did you change the model?”)
- Harder support escalations (no single place to point)
- Enterprise change-management blockers (FinchBank/HelIOHealth style approvals)

We need a customer-visible, canonical changelog surfaced in Console, docs, and machine-readable endpoints—generated from a single source of truth and governed by an approval workflow.

2) Goals / non-goals
Goals (MVP)
- Console: customers can view model release notes (changelog) per model + per version, with filters and stable share links.
- Console: rollouts pages can reference the exact changelog entry relevant at the time of a rollout or pin change.
- Provide export options that unblock enterprise change-management processes (at minimum: CSV + PDF print view; JSON feed handled separately but linked).
- Internal workflow: draft -> in_review -> published with RBAC + audit trail.
- Launch stages: private beta (select accounts) -> public beta -> GA.

Non-goals (MVP)
- Auto-generated narrative quality diffs (we will link eval dashboards/metrics where available).
- Per-customer customized notes.
- Real-time streaming events to customers (daily batch acceptable).

3) Personas & primary user stories
Personas
A) ML engineer / app engineer (self-serve): wants to understand “what changed” and whether pinned versions are still supported.
B) Platform / release manager (enterprise): needs auditable, immutable notes to attach to internal approvals.
C) Support/CSM: needs a single URL to resolve “behavior changed” complaints.

User stories (Console)
US-1: As a customer, I can open a model page and view a “Changelog” tab listing recent updates.
US-2: As a customer, I can filter notes by date range and by version (e.g., show only entries affecting version 2026-02-10).
US-3: As a customer, I can export or print release notes for internal review.
US-4: As an enterprise customer, I can share a stable URL with my internal stakeholders that won’t change content silently.
US-5: As a customer, I can understand compatibility impacts (API surface, tool/function calling, context window, deployment modes).
US-6: As a customer, I can see deprecation timelines + replacement guidance.

User stories (Internal)
INT-1: As Release Eng/Product, I can review/edit customer-safe wording before publish.
INT-2: As Security/Compliance, I can audit who published or edited what fields and when.
INT-3: As Support, I can flag an entry as confusing/incorrect and trigger a correction path that preserves audit history.

4) Scope overview (Console)
4.1 Entry points
- Model Catalog (Console): each model card/list row links to Model Detail.
- Model Detail page: add “Changelog” tab.
- Model Version page (if separate view exists): show version-level changelog subset + link back to model-level.
- Rollouts page: show “Related release note” link(s) for model version transitions.

4.2 Model page “Changelog” tab — requirements
List view
- Default sort: newest first.
- Each row (changelog entry) shows:
  - Date/time (customer locale; include UTC timestamp in detail view)
  - Change type badge (taxonomy from PM-801): Add / Update / Deprecation / Fix / Performance / Compatibility / Policy/Safety (final set TBD)
  - A short customer_safe_summary (1–2 lines)
  - Affected version(s): version_id(s) and “current default” indicator if applicable
  - Deployment availability chips: Hosted / Dedicated / Private (only show if relevant)
  - Status indicator only for internal view (draft/in_review/published); customers only see published

Detail view
- Clicking an entry opens a detail drawer or dedicated page (TBD w/ Design). Must support a stable URL.
- Sections (customer-visible template, see style guide alignment w/ Docs team):
  1) Summary
  2) Impact (what you might observe)
  3) Compatibility notes (API/tool calling/structured output/context window; also any “no changes” callouts)
  4) Deprecation (if applicable): dates, affected endpoints, replacement model/version
  5) Links: docs page, eval dashboard link (if present), rollback guidance link
  6) Metadata footer: entry_id, published_at, last_updated_at (if corrections happen), and “This entry is immutable; corrections are published as a new entry referencing the prior one” language

Filtering & search
- Date range filter: last 7/30/90 days + custom.
- Version filter:
  - Multi-select version_id(s)
  - “Show entries impacting my pinned version” (reads resolved version for the account/project/workspace; depends on how pinning is modeled)
- Change type filter (multi-select)
- Deployment mode filter (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) — only show if customer has access
- Text search: matches summary + version_id + model_id (basic; no full semantic search in MVP)

Pagination
- Infinite scroll acceptable, but must support shareable filtered URLs.
- Performance target: first paint < 2s for 50 entries, and reasonable for 500 entries with pagination.

Export / share
- “Copy link” on entry detail view: stable permalink.
- “Export list” actions (MVP):
  - CSV export of current filtered list (date, change_type, summary, affected_versions, published_at, permalink)
  - Print/PDF-friendly view for a single entry (browser print works; we provide a minimal print stylesheet)
- Post-MVP: JSON export from Console UI (likely redundant with public feed endpoint but requested by some accounts).

Access / tenant rules
- Only show entries for models available to the account tier/region.
- For model variants restricted to certain contracts (Dedicated/Private), only show those notes if the account is entitled.

4.3 Rollouts integration — requirements
- On Rollouts history detail, show the relevant published changelog entry for the version change (or the closest matching entry if multiple).
- If no entry exists (e.g., historical pre-migration), show a clear placeholder: “Release note unavailable for this date; see Known Gaps.”
- Provide a support-focused copy button: “Copy support link” that includes model/version + entry permalink.

5) Approval workflow & governance (internal)
We need a lightweight but auditable workflow. Proposed states (aligning with Eng endpoints work):
- draft: auto-generated by pipeline from model registry change-event. Editable by allowed roles.
- in_review: locked for editing except “reviewer notes” fields; reviewers can request changes.
- published: customer-visible; immutable.
- superseded: if we correct wording, we publish a new entry that references the previous one. The previous remains visible with a banner: “Superseded by ENTRY_ID on DATE.” (We need Design input.)

Roles (high-level; exact RBAC handled by Platform/Security)
- Editors: Product + Release Eng + Docs (limited set) can edit customer_safe fields on drafts.
- Approvers: Product lead (Marissa) + Release Eng lead (Connor) required for publish of certain change types (deprecations/policy/safety).
- Emergency publish: on-call Release Eng can publish with retroactive approval within 1 business day (must be audited).
- Support: can flag an entry as confusing/incorrect; cannot edit published content.

Required review gates
- Any deprecation requires:
  - sunset_date present
  - replacement_model/version present (or explicit “no replacement available”)
  - timeline conforms to change-management policy
- Any compatibility-affecting change requires a Compatibility section (even if “No customer action required”).
- Any performance update should avoid specific internal hardware details; if we include perf deltas, they must be “observed typical” and include caveats.

Audit requirements (customer-facing expectations)
- Publish actions and edits must be attributed and timestamped.
- Customers should be able to reference entry_id and published_at in tickets.

6) UX requirements for internal reviewers (Console)
Internal view toggle (only for Redwood staff)
- Changelog entry list shows status column, “needs review” badge, and SLA timers (e.g., “in review for 2d”).
- Entry detail includes:
  - Diff summary: what fields changed in registry event (internal)
  - Customer-safe template preview
  - Edit fields: summary, impact, compatibility notes, deprecation messaging, links
  - Validation warnings (e.g., missing required sections)
  - Buttons: Submit for review, Request changes, Approve & publish, Publish (emergency)

Notes
- This PRD does not define the exact editing UI; could be a separate “Release notes” tool. But product preference is “in Console” to reduce context switching.

7) Content rules / style constraints (customer-safe)
We must avoid:
- Internal model nicknames
- Vendor-sensitive details (unless explicitly public/contracted)
- Unverified claims about accuracy/safety improvements
- Anything that implies customer data was used unless explicitly covered and approved

We should include:
- Clear “customer impact” language (“No action required” vs “Consider pinning version X”)
- Compatibility and deprecation timelines
- Links to docs and to eval dashboards when available

Docs alignment
- Console and docs site should display the same published text from the same source.

8) Launch plan (phased rollout)
Stage 0 — Internal dogfood
- Enable internal-only view + publish pipeline in staging.
- Validate workflow, audit logs, and docs sync.
- Success: <5% publish failures; review SLA <2 business days for normal entries.

Stage 1 — Private beta (enterprise design partners)
- Feature flag on Console “Changelog” tab for select accounts.
- Candidate accounts (not exhaustive): FinchBank, HelioHealth, StackForge (see GTM notes).
- Provide onboarding doc + feedback form.
- Success metrics:
  - At least 3 accounts actively using changelog tab weekly
  - Reduction in “model changed without notice” tickets for beta accounts (qualitative + tagged)

Stage 2 — Public beta
- Changelog tab visible for all accounts, but export features may remain gated.
- RSS/Atom + JSON feed announced (if ready; otherwise provide “coming soon” with docs).
- Success: support team uses permalinks in >50% of relevant tickets.

Stage 3 — GA
- Remove beta label.
- Add change-management docs references across Hosted/Dedicated/Private docs.
- Publish formal SLA/expectations for deprecation notice windows.

9) Success metrics
Quantitative
- Support: decrease in tickets tagged “unannounced model change” (baseline from Jan–Feb).
- Adoption: % of active workspaces that view changelog tab monthly.
- Export usage: number of CSV exports / print views (proxy for enterprise workflows).
- Publish lag: median time from registry change-event -> published entry.

Qualitative
- Enterprise security reviews: fewer custom questionnaires about “how do you communicate model changes” once changelog exists.
- CSM feedback: fewer escalations during rollouts.

10) Open questions / decisions needed
- Taxonomy finalization (PM-801): do we separate “Performance” vs “Fix”, and do we show “Policy/Safety” as a top-level category?
- Filters: should version filter be by version_id only, or support semantic “major/minor”? (Probably version_id only for v1.)
- Permalink format: /models/{model_id}/changelog/{entry_id} vs /changelog/{entry_id}. Need stable + shareable + permission-safe.
- Export: do we need PDF generation server-side for enterprise (vs print stylesheet)? (MVP: print.)
- Rollouts mapping: how do we deterministically attach an entry to a rollout when multiple events happen in a day?
- Backfill and “known gaps”: what do we show for pre-migration history? Need a consistent UX message.

11) Appendix — customer inputs (high signal)
- SUP-18421: Enterprise asks for immutable release notes + retention/audit language.
- SUP-18473: Requests RSS/API feed of model updates.
- SUP-18502: Changelog wording confusion; wants clearer customer impact + compatibility notes.

Notes to self (Marissa)
- Confirm which Console surfaces are “workspace-scoped” vs “org-scoped” for pinning. The “my pinned version” filter may require a first pass at how we read resolved version state.
- Need Dev Patel + Support readiness plan: canned responses + how to reference entry_id in tickets.
